cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: Dark matter makes up ~27% of the universe's mass-energy; it does not emit, absorb or reflect light

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: Evidence for dark matter: galaxy rotation curves (stars orbit faster than expected), gravitational lensing, galaxy cluster dynamics

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: Dark energy makes up ~68% of the universe's mass-energy; it drives the accelerating expansion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: Ordinary (baryonic) matter makes up only ~5% of the universe

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: Dark energy was discovered through observations of distant Type Ia supernovae showing the expansion is accelerating

cards.front: Recall a key point about Dark Matter & Dark Energy
cards.back: The fate of the universe depends on the balance of matter and dark energy

cards.front: What should you know about gcse astronomy exam tips — dark matter & dark energy?
cards.back: 1. For Dark Matter & Dark Energy questions, define key terms before explaining processes 2. Use 'because' to link cause and effect in your explanations 3. Include units in all calculations and show your working for method marks 4. When evaluating Dark Matter & Dark Energy, consider both the quality of evidence and practical implications 5. For extended response questions, plan your answer: identify AO1/AO2/AO3 requirements first
